title: HTMLInputElement type=url “absolute URL string” constraint-validation-API requirements don’t match actual Gecko/Blink/WebKit implementation behavior

labels.name: compat
labels.description: Standard is not web compatible or proprietary feature needs standardizing

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#url-state-(type=url) contains this requirement:

> Constraint validation: While the [value](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#concept-fe-value) of the element is neither the empty string nor a [valid](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-url-string) [absolute URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute), the element is [suffering from a type mismatch](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#suffering-from-a-type-mismatch).

…where “absolute URL” is https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute — and, notably, is not [“absolute-URL-with-fragment string”](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#absolute-url-with-fragment-string).

So, the spec as currently written disallows every URL-like-string that contains any fragment part at all.

And the spec also disallows every URL-like-string that contains any literal ASCII-whitespace code points.

And further, the spec disallows certain characters in various parts of the URL-like-string — even in cases where a conforming URL parser will parse that string into an actual URL, in spite of the “disallowed” characters.

However, none of WebKit/Gecko/Blink actually disallow any of those things in values for `type=url` `input` elements.

Instead — based on examining the results of the additional test cases in https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/51011/files — all that WebKit/Gecko/Blink appearing to be doing is:

1. They run their URL parsers on the input URL-like-string values of `type=url` `input` elements.
2. As long as the parser successfully returns a URL object with a value, they treat the input URL-like-string values as valid.
